 Seven in 10 sunscreens fail SPF claims in New Zealand test
 Seven in 10 sunscreens fail SPF claims in New Zealand test
 30-Oct-2026, 13:07 30 Oct 2026, 13:07 Bernama Share The findings highlighted the need for regular independent testing in a country with one of the world's highest skin cancer and melanoma rates.
 One sunscreen labelled SPF50 was found to provide protection equivalent to just SPF14. (Envato Elements pic) 
 WELLINGTON : Seven out of 10 sunscreens tested by New Zealand’s consumer advocacy group failed to meet their advertised sun protection factor (SPF) claims, with one product labelled SPF50 providing protection equivalent to just SPF14, reported Xinhua. 
 Consumer NZ tested 10 widely available sunscreens, of which only three met their SPF label claims.
 However, all 10 met broad-spectrum protection requirements based on their tested SPF levels, the group said in a statement on Friday.
 “New Zealand has one of the highest skin cancer and melanoma rates in the world,” said Consumer NZ researcher Belinda Castles, who noted that sunscreen plays an important role in preventing skin cancer.
 The findings highlighted the need for regular independent sunscreen testing, as there are no rules specifying how often sunscreens must be tested, Consumer NZ said.
 Previous investigations by the group had found that some companies relied on test reports that were several years old.
